history: How can I compare the metrics for different periods?

To compare the metrics for different periods, you can use the Time period control to select the desired time frames. You can choose from predefined periods such as a single day, a week, a month, or a quarter, or create custom time periods. The data points on the graph will adjust to an appropriate measurement period for the selected time frame. For example, when viewing a graph for a day, the data is presented in hourly values, but when viewing a graph for a week, the data is shown by day. Additionally, you can use the Refresh data option to ensure the data is up-to-date.

For instance, you can set an alert to trigger when CPU usage exceeds 80% for at least 5 minutes. - Notification Channel: Enable 1 or more notification channels to receive alert notifications. Remember to save your alert settings after configuring them. For more information, refer to the document on configuring alerts: [Configuring an alert](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/monitoring?topic=monitoring-alert-config).
I cannot get select query to work, what steps should I take?

1. Check if you have the correct access rights: You need at least 'Reader' access to the buckets that contain the input objects. 2. After the FROM keyword, specify one or more unique resource identifiers (URIs) which can be thought of as tables. Each URI can specify one or more input objects, which can also be thought of as table partitions. 3. If the format of the input objects is CSV, and no special options are required, it is not necessary to specify a STORED AS clause. However, if the format is JSON, ORC, Parquet, or AVRO, after the FROM clause, specify STORED AS JSON, STORED AS ORC, STORED AS PARQUET, or STORED AS AVRO. 4. If text formats, such as JSON and CSV, are compressed with either gzip or bzip2 and have the extensions .gz and .bz, they automatically get recognized as compressed files. However, do not use these kinds of compressed files due to performance reasons. 5. If the format of the input objects is CSV and a delimiter other than the default , (comma) is used, you must specify the delimiter by using the FIELDS TERMINATED BY option of the STORED AS clause. All single Unicode characters are allowed as delimiters. 6. Check for a header line: By default, it is assumed that CSV input objects have a header line that specifies the names of the input columns.
